summary: Verified vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript patterns for Sage's responsive drawer, in-flow bottom composer, fetch-based SSE parsing, and server-owned session-title flow. No source files were modified.

findings.conclusion: MDN documents matchMedia() as both an instantaneous media-query check and a change-event source. Use one MediaQueryList such as matchMedia('(max-width: 1023px)') as the source of truth instead of comparing innerWidth only when the menu is clicked. On a change to desktop, close the mobile backdrop, remove inertness, and restore the desktop open state; on a change to mobile, keep the drawer closed unless the user explicitly opened it. A throttled window resize handler is appropriate for layout measurements because resize can fire frequently.

Keep the desktop sidebar in normal flex layout and make the narrow version an overlay drawer with a stable state class or data attribute. Give the menu button aria-controls pointing at the sidebar and aria-expanded reflecting state. Use transform or an equivalent visual transition rather than changing width to zero; keep the drawer scrollable independently. The current Sage pages put the sidebar at position:absolute with top:0 inside .layout but do not make .layout positioned, so the containing block and overlay extent are fragile; add position:relative to .layout and use inset-block:0/inset-inline-start:0 for the drawer. Use a real labelled close button or a non-focusable backdrop layer.

If the mobile drawer blocks the workspace, make the workspace inert while it is open, close on Escape and backdrop activation, move focus into the drawer, and return focus to the menu button on close. MDN states inert removes an element and descendants from focus, click handling, and the accessibility tree; native dialog showModal() provides modal inertness and Escape behavior, but an aside with explicit state is usually simpler for this drawer. Do not apply modal behavior to the persistent desktop sidebar.

In static/sage-workspace.html and sibling pages, the mobile drawer is toggled by class and backdrop but has no resize or breakpoint-change synchronization, Escape path, focus return, or aria-expanded/aria-controls state. app.js has a separate sidebar implementation and no backdrop wiring. Consolidate drawer state per page or share one vanilla module; otherwise resize can leave a stale backdrop or drawer state.
findings.source: static/sage-workspace.html lines 23-36 and 207-217; static/app.js lines 564-570 (repository inspection)

findings.conclusion: For the chat, use an in-flow composer as the final child of a height-constrained column: .chat { display:flex; flex-direction:column; min-height:0; }, .chat__messages { flex:1 1 auto; min-height:0; overflow:auto; }, .input-bar { flex:0 0 auto; }. min-height:0 on nested flex items that own the scrolling child permits the transcript to shrink instead of forcing the composer below the viewport. Avoid position:fixed unless equivalent bottom padding is deliberately maintained.

findings.topic: Mobile viewport height and keyboard constraints
findings.conclusion: Use min-height:100dvh with a fallback such as 100svh or 100vh. MDN distinguishes dynamic viewport units, which track browser UI changes, from small viewport units, which are the safer stable minimum. Add padding-block-end:calc(0.75rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)) to the composer. VisualViewport exposes height and resize because the on-screen keyboard can shrink the visual viewport without changing the layout viewport; listen to visualViewport.resize only when JavaScript must react to the keyboard, preferring CSS for ordinary layout.

Sage already has .chat as a column flex container, .chat__messages as flex:1 with overflow:auto, and .input-bar as flex-shrink:0. Add min-height:0 to .chat and .chat__messages, use a dynamic/small viewport height on .app, and include safe-area bottom padding. Keep textarea max-height and overflow:auto so expansion cannot consume the mobile viewport. Keep .chat__messages as the intended scroller while html/body remain overflow:hidden.

The WHATWG HTML Standard requires text/event-stream to be UTF-8 and permits CRLF, LF, or CR line endings. A blank line dispatches an event; colon-prefixed lines are comments; data fields append values separated by LF; unknown fields are ignored. A fetch reader must retain a carry-over buffer between chunks, split all three line-ending forms, parse complete event blocks only at a blank line, ignore heartbeat comments, and treat an EOF in the middle of an event as incomplete rather than successful.

MDN states response.body is a ReadableStream, getReader() locks it, chunks can split arbitrarily, and TextDecoderStream can decode UTF-8 incrementally. Check response.ok before reading, then use response.body.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()) where available or TextDecoder.decode(value,{stream:true}) otherwise. Release or cancel the reader in finally and abort with AbortController for Stop. Never read the same response body through both text/json and the reader because consumption disturbs the stream.

Sage app/sse.py emits data: JSON followed by a blank line, with the application discriminator in JSON property type. turn.py emits type values meta, delta, citation, done, and error; heartbeat emits : ping comments. The current static/app.js parser checks ev.event, so it ignores normal application events, then unconditionally calls onDone({}) at EOF. Dispatch on ev.type, ignore comments, and never synthesize done merely because the network stream ended.
findings.source: app/sse.py lines 12-15 and 18-46; app/services/sessions/turn.py lines 76-89, 106-135, and 220-231; static/app.js lines 117-143 (repository inspection)

findings.conclusion: Use one terminal guard and one accumulated response object per turn. meta updates source previews/insufficient state; delta appends to final_text exactly once and re-renders one assistant node; citation adds chunk_id to a Set; done records identifiers and commits accumulated final_text; error records code/message/retryable but preserves text already received. Ignore unknown types. EOF before done marks the assistant partial/interrupted and retains text; duplicate done is ignored. A replayed done may contain no content, so refresh GET /api/sessions/{id} when local content is absent or reconciliation is needed.

FastAPI documents StreamingResponse as accepting an async generator and streaming its yielded body, and confirms SSE works over POST. Sage's custom StreamingResponse with text/event-stream, no-cache, X-Accel-Buffering:no, and 15-second comment heartbeats is a valid fit. Use fetch rather than EventSource for the existing POST turn endpoint because EventSource does not provide a POST request body.

FastAPI's request-body documentation confirms a Pydantic model is read as JSON, validated, and returned as JSON. Sage POST /api/sessions accepts SessionCreate, whose goal has min_length=1, and returns a Session containing id and title. static/app.js createSession currently posts {goal: ''}, which violates validation; the client must not create an empty session under the current API.
findings.source: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/body/; app/models.py lines 29-33 and app/api/sessions.py lines 26-34; static/app.js lines 484-493 (repository inspection)

findings.conclusion: SessionService.create assigns title=goal[:80] on the server and returns the persisted Session. This is server-owned deterministic truncation, not LLM-generated semantic titling. The vanilla client should POST a valid initial goal, capture response.id and response.title, update header/sidebar from that response, and use the returned id for the turn. Do not derive or overwrite the title in browser state. True generated titles require a separate server-side title-generation step or endpoint.
findings.source: app/services/sessions/session.py lines 30-57 and 171-187; app/models.py lines 35-48 (repository inspection)

findings.conclusion: For the current API: collect the first non-empty composer text; POST /api/sessions with {goal:first_text,file_ids:[],grounding_mode:'grounded'}; await JSON; set session_id from response.id, title from response.title, and URL state; insert the user message; then POST /api/sessions/{id}/turns with the same text and a unique crypto.randomUUID client_msg_id; parse the stream. If a blank draft is required, the FastAPI model and service must be changed in a separate server task because a client-only workaround cannot satisfy validation.
findings.source: app/api/sessions.py lines 26-34; app/models.py lines 29-33; app/services/sessions/session.py lines 30-57; https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/body/

recommendations: For all static pages, create one drawer state function owning class/data-state, aria-expanded, aria-controls, backdrop visibility, body scroll lock, workspace inertness, focus-in, focus-return, and Escape handling. Use matchMedia('(max-width: 1023px)') change plus a debounced resize fallback; reconcile state on breakpoint changes instead of only toggling on clicks.

Set .layout { position:relative; } and use an overlay drawer with inset-block:0 and inset-inline-start:0. Keep desktop sidebar width in flex flow; at the narrow breakpoint use transform/visibility/pointer-events state. Prefer a labelled close button or button backdrop and synchronize ARIA state.

Treat the mobile drawer as modal only while open: set main.inert, lock document scrolling, focus the first drawer control, close on Escape/backdrop, then remove inert and return focus to #menu-btn. Do not apply inert or modal behavior to the persistent desktop sidebar.

Keep the composer in flow as the last child of the chat column. Set .app min-height:100dvh with a fallback, .chat min-height:0, .chat__messages flex:1 1 auto;min-height:0;overflow:auto, and .input-bar flex:0 0 auto with padding-bottom:calc(var(--space-5) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px)). Cap textarea height and let it scroll internally.

Implement a standalone parse_sse_stream(response, handlers, signal) helper around response.body and a streaming UTF-8 decoder. Parse CRLF/LF/CR, blank-line event blocks, multi-line data, and colon comments. Validate response.ok/content type and release or cancel the reader in finally.

Dispatch Sage application events by parsed JSON.type, not JSON.event. Handle meta, delta, citation, done, and error; ignore ping comments and unknown types. Use final_text as the sole accumulated assistant content, a Set for citations, one terminal guard, no unconditional onDone at EOF, and preserve partial text on error, abort, or incomplete EOF.

For replayed done events with no local content, GET /api/sessions/{session_id} and reconcile persisted messages. Never replace accumulated text with an empty done payload. Treat EOF without done as interrupted rather than successful.

Implement New chat as a first-message transaction against the current API: require non-empty text, POST /api/sessions with that text as goal, use returned id/title, then start the turn using the same text and a unique client_msg_id. Do not post goal:'', and do not generate titles in vanilla JS. If true LLM titles are required, change the server contract separately.

Keep the existing FastAPI StreamingResponse and POST SSE endpoint. Add client tests for chunks split inside UTF-8 characters, JSON lines, CRLF/LF/CR, comments, duplicate terminal events, error after deltas, EOF before done, and replayed done.
notes: Research was read-only. Sources were retrieved from official MDN, WHATWG HTML, and FastAPI documentation, then compared with the existing vanilla static client and FastAPI implementation. No source files were modified. Existing T1.json was replaced with this Hermes research log because the requested task explicitly names T1.json as the deliverable.
